_readme: Every permanent, account-wide Divine Principality upgrade. Edit this file, then run Prince's Palace > Build Default Content. id is written into save data as a purchase (SaveData.purchasedUpgradeIds), so NEVER rename one after a save exists -- a save drops any purchase whose id no longer resolves, so a rename reads to the player as a refund they did not ask for. UpgradeEntryResolver refuses a duplicate id, a missing displayName, a negative cost and a negative startingGoldBonus at build time, and nothing is written for the whole type when any row fails, because a catalogue that merely lost a row is the quietest possible failure. DELIBERATELY SEPARATE FROM TALENTS: talents are per-character build power bought with a run's own progression, these are profile-wide and bought with Principality currency, so the two never compete for the same pot. SHOP ORDER IS FILE ORDER: sortOrder is assigned from position here, because Resources.LoadAll returns filename order and that would silently reshuffle the shop (CLAUDE.md gotcha 4). ONE ROW TODAY. starting_gold_boost is the only user of startingGoldBonus and the field exists for it: the field is authored but no run-start code reads it yet; the intent is an in-run currency grant through that number rather than a case in code, so a second gold upgrade is a row and not a branch. The extra_recruit_slot row was removed: the squad is capped at the stage's three slots, so it changed nothing; a save that bought it drops the purchase on load. Costs are first-pass and unbalanced -- there is no Principality shop screen yet, so nothing has ever charged anybody 30 for anything. Field-by-field documentation, defaults and valid enum values: docs/CONTENT_SCHEMA.md.

upgrades.description: Begin each run with extra gold.
